collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A young healer wants to try an unfamiliar herb: ask the old plant gatherer first, or test it carefully alone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found a plant with silver leaves that (subject.he/she) thinks might ease fevers. (friend), the oldest plant gatherer, knows every leaf on the island, but (subject) has always found (friend.him/her) gruff and secretive. Should (subject) ask (friend), or test the plant (subject.him/her)self, carefully?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) takes one look and laughs. The silver leaf eases fevers, (friend.he/she) says, but only the young leaves; the old ones cause a terrible stomach ache. (friend.He/she) spends the afternoon showing (subject) how to tell the difference. Gruff, but generous.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tries a tiny amount on (subject.him/her)self first. (subject.He/she) spends the night with a terrible stomach ache. In the morning, (friend) shuffles in, looks at (subject.him/her), and says, "Old leaves." (subject) learns more from that than from anything.
